A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InterRetro research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark success rates, route lengths, sample-efficiency experiments, ablations, and generated molecular routes in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results in Section 5, Tables 1–2, Figure 4, and the molecular case studies in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The stated policy loss gains a minus sign: v1 Eq. 15 becomes the negative weighted log-likelihood in v2 Eq. 16, consistent with loss minimization. Algorithm 1, architecture, and other updates remain unchanged; this correction does not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same stated USPTO-50k training molecules, eMolecules building blocks, and Retro*-190, ChEMBL-1000, and GDB17-1000 evaluation coverage. Removing brief dataset descriptions does not change the evaluated populations or tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in both tables. Table 1 retains the same single-step/search combinations, while Table 2 retains Retro*, RetroGraph, PDVN, MEGAN, and Graph2Edits. Two revised scores do not change the comparator set.

E3.justification: Both versions report direct generation and 100/200/500 model-call budgets, the same 138-target route-length subset, training-data fractions, and advantage-coefficient settings. No revised evaluation procedure or training budget is reported.

E4.justification: The sample-efficiency study, depth-estimation analysis, and advantage-coefficient ablation retain identical Figure 4 plots. The same three molecular case studies move from v1 Appendix B/Figure 6 to v2 Appendix A/Figure 5.

E5.justification: Figure 4 retains identical boxplots and shaded learning curves. Neither version supplies additional run counts, seeds, uncertainty definitions, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures relative to the other.

E6.justification: For Retro*-190 at 500 model calls, Table 1 changes Template+Retro* from 79.47% to 75.26% and Self-improve+Retro* from 96.32% to 94.74%. InterRetro scores, Table 2 route lengths, and empirical plots remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain these score revisions.

T1.justification: V2 removes v1 Appendix A's explicit best-path action-value definition and worked mathematical comparison with worst-path optimization, including Eqs. 17–18. The main Bellman relations, contraction result, and policy-improvement proofs remain substantively unchanged, with proofs moving from Appendix C to B.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same contributions: worst-path optimization, weighted self-imitation, optimality and monotonic-improvement guarantees, and search-free planning. The headline claims of 100% benchmark success, approximately 4.9% shorter routes, and strong performance using 10% of training data are unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 revises future directions toward reaction conditions, building-block costs, and feasibility checks, dropping alternative depth/search proposals. Its rewritten Broader Impacts discussion replaces v1 Appendix E's sustainability and deployment-risk discussion with a Responsible Use License proposal. The central practical-feasibility limitation remains.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 replaces a promise of future code release with stated open-source availability and a concrete repository link. Hardware, training time, exploration processes, update counts, and Graph2Edits details remain unchanged; the 20,000-branch buffer is clarified as a maximum capacity.

R1.justification: V2 removes Section 2's dedicated comparison with Schreck et al. [21], which positioned InterRetro against earlier reinforcement-learning retrosynthesis and contrasted their objectives and action selection. The same 39 referenced works remain, and the broader positioning is retained.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted explanatory rewrites, renames Value Estimation to Advantage Estimation, standardizes tree terminology, and corrects proof headings. It removes the worked-example appendix, integrates rewritten broader impacts into the main discussion, and adds acknowledgments while preserving the main section sequence.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the NeurIPS template, changing typography, title formatting, margins, and spacing throughout. Figures and tables are extensively reflowed, Table 2 becomes a wrapped display beside text, and the illustrative tree-comparison figure is removed. Retained empirical graphics are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The corrected policy-loss sign resolves a specification inconsistency, and the concrete code link improves reproducibility information over v1's release promise. These limited gains outweigh the loss of the worked example and some explicit related-work context. Experimental support and core proofs remain essentially unchanged; the revised baseline scores alone do not establish improved quality.
